case_title: Ajitsingh Harnamsingh Gujral v. State of Maharashtra
accused_age: Not stated (High Court described him as around 50 to 52 years at the time; no single age given)
accused_socioeconomic_status: Businessman with several employees and a car; had suffered business losses earlier at Ludhiana
victim_age: Not stated (four victims; son about 20, daughters about 22 and 13, wife's age not given)
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (wife); Relative: father of the son and two daughters who were killed
weapon: Petrol poured with a red bucket (petrol can also found in the flat)
evidence_type: Circumstantial (no eyewitnesses); last-seen evidence; witness testimony on quarrels and dictatorial conduct; recovery under s.27 Evidence Act; chemical analyser report; panchanama of petrol can
confession: Section 27 disclosure statement by the accused pointing out the red bucket; relied on by the Court (not a confession to the killing)
aggravating_circumstances: Burning of four family members while asleep; gruesome, diabolical manner; pre-planned with large quantity of petrol brought into flat; victims were family members; accused absconded afterwards
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC for four murders; death sentence imposed
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 (four counts: wife, son and two daughters)
neutral_facts: In the early hours of 10 April 2003, a fire broke out in the residential flat where the accused lived with his wife and three children. Witnesses testified that the accused and his wife were heard quarrelling loudly at about midnight on the previous night, and that the accused was seen returning to the flat around that time. The accused's family had a history of tension, and witnesses described the accused as a dictatorial and hot-tempered man who had beaten his wife with a leather belt and whose children resented his behaviour. Household servants sleeping in the veranda heard a loud noise at about 4.00 to 4.30 a.m. and found the flat on fire with a strong smell of petrol. After the fire was extinguished, the bodies of the wife, son and two daughters were found burnt in the children's bedroom. A witness had earlier seen a new ten-litre plastic can containing petrol in the flat. The accused's car was missing and he was not found at the scene. Police later recovered a red bucket from the flat's bathroom on the accused's own disclosure, and a chemical analysis of the bucket showed the presence of petrol. The electrician who inspected the premises found no short circuit. Post-mortem examinations showed that all four victims died from burning. The accused's own account of having left to visit a sick relative was not accepted by the investigators.
offence_severity: Death or imprisonment for life, and fine (no separate fine amount stated)
physical_harm: Death of four persons (wife, son and two daughters) by burning; son had incised injuries, explained by broken glass
number_of_offences: 1 charged (IPC s.302, four counts); 1 finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Yes: Court found the murder pre-planned, not on spur of the moment, because a large quantity of petrol was brought into the flat
motive: Not identified (Court held motive could only be speculated; marital strain and quarrels were found but no motive was fixed)
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of PW3, PW4, PW5 and PW16 on midnight quarrel and last seen; testimony on dictatorial conduct and leather belt beatings; 10-litre petrol can found in flat; red bucket recovered on disclosure and tested positive for petrol; false alibi; accused's flight
witness_credibility: PW3 (brother-in-law), PW5 (mother-in-law), PW4 and PW16 found credible; no enmity or motive to lie shown against them
post_offence_conduct: Left the scene and was found with cash and safari dresses in Rajasthan; put forward an alibi of visiting a sick sister in Delhi, found false by the Court
trial_duration: offence: 10.4.2003; trial judgment: 19.3.2005; High Court: 26.6.2006; Supreme Court: 13.9.2011
legal_representation: Appellant: Jaspal Singh (senior counsel), Aman Vachher, Ashutosh Dubey, L.K. Sharma (for P.N. Puri). State of Maharashtra: Sushil Karanjkar (for Asha Gopalan Nair)
investigation_status: Report lodged by PSI; inquest, spot panchanama and post mortem done; accused arrested 14.4.2003; charge sheet filed; trial completed with 19 prosecution witnesses
procedural_irregularity: None noted (Court found 168 questions put under s.313 Cr.P.C., so the defence objection was rejected)
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302, death sentence. High Court: appeal dismissed, death sentence upheld. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Case rested on a chain of circumstances: last seen with the wife, petrol brought into flat, bucket recovered, false alibi and flight; the Court's summary of the prosecution case is recorded, with no separate State submissions detailed
defence_argument: No motive proved and a happy married life of 25 years; the bucket was a police fabrication; alibi of visiting sick sister in Delhi; s.313 questions not put; injuries on son unexplained; petrol-splashing and bodies-on-ground inconsistencies
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence: complete chain of circumstances must point to accused; last-seen theory; s.114 Evidence Act natural conduct; rarest of rare test with Macchi Singh balance sheet
precedent_relied_upon: Wakkar v. State of UP (2011) 3 SCC 306; Krishnan (2008) 15 SCC 430; Sharad Birdhichand Sarda AIR 1984 SC 1622; Mohd. Mannan (2011) 5 SCC 317; Mohd. Azad (2008) 15 SCC 449; Mahender Singh Dahiya (2011) 3 SCC 109; S.K. Yusuf JT 2011 (6) SC 640; Santosh v. State of MP AIR 1975 SC 654; Bachan Singh AIR 1980 SC 898; Machhi Singh AIR 1983 SC 957; Common Cause (2008) 5 SCC 511
sentencing_rationale: Burning living persons is a horrible act causing excruciating pain; pre-planned; accused cannot be reformed or rehabilitated; balance sheet heavily against him; falls within rarest of rare cases
judicial_aggravating_factors: Pre-planned, cruel and barbaric killing of his own family; burning of living persons; no provocation; accused cannot be reformed
